items.title: Kent Nagano, director de la Orquesta Nacional de España: “Rosalía va más allá del pop, sería un sueño colaborar con ella”
items.description: Cuando Kent Nagano (Berkeley, California, 74 años) les dijo a sus padres que quería dedicarse a la música no lo apoyaron. Extraña en quien tocaba el piano desde los cuatro años como parte de un programa educativo rigurosamente aplicado por su madre en casa. Pero, a la hora de la verdad, no vieron claro que siguiera esa vocación prendida con esfuerzo de manera vital. Por eso pensó durante un tiempo que podía buscar una alternativa en el mundo del derecho y la diplomacia. Finalmente, impuso su voluntad en el entorno estricto de un clan familiar japonés cuyos ancestros se habían instalado como granjeros a finales del siglo XIX en el oeste de Estados Unidos. Con empeño, pese al rechazo, acabó por desarrollar una carrera estelar que empezó en Boston, pasó por bares y compañías de ballet como acompañante para buscar recursos con que mantenerse y ha acabado como uno de los más firmes referentes de la dirección de orquesta del mundo después de haber pasado como titular por la Sinfónica de Montreal, la Ópera Estatal de Baviera o la Filarmónica de Hamburgo. En su trayectoria siempre buscó puentes y conexiones entre la gran música y las tendencias populares. Ha colaborado con Frank Zappa, Sting, Björk y no le importaría, asegura, hacerlo en esta nueva etapa con Rosalía. Estudioso profundo de Mahler —debutará con su Segunda sinfonía en Madrid el 18, 19 y 20 de septiembre—, devoto de Wagner y el repertorio francés y alemán, entregado y comprometido con la música contemporánea, Nagano ha descubierto que la música y la diplomacia van de la mano. De hecho, le gustaría hacer de la Orquesta Nacional una embajadora de buenas vibraciones por el mundo. Este mes llegará a las librerías la biografía Kent Nagano. 10 lecciones en mi vida , escrita por Inge Kloepfer y editada por Alianza. Seguir leyendo

items.title: David Szalay, escritor: “El sexo y la violencia son experiencias no verbales. Por eso cuesta tanto escribir sobre ellas”
items.description: Es un hombre tranquilo, con aspecto de amar la soledad y el silencio, al que el mayor premio de las letras inglesas ha trastocado un poco la existencia. David Szalay (Montreal, 1974) ganó el último Booker con La carne (Feltrinelli, con traducción de Ce Santiago), una novela que comprime varias décadas en la vida de un húngaro aparentemente corriente —aunque su libro demuestra que ninguna vida lo es del todo— entre la caída del comunismo, la guerra de Irak, la entrada de su país en la Unión Europea, el Londres del Brexit y el cataclismo de la pandemia. El estruendo del Booker se ha visto atenuado por su lugar de residencia: Viena , donde vive con su esposa y su hijo de dos años, lejos de los focos más cegadores. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “Busco mujer para sexo después de misa”: cuando encontrábamos pareja a través de los anuncios por palabras
items.description: “Hombre de 28 años, de excelente familia, de agradable apariencia, con buenas perspectivas, desea casarse con una joven con dote.” Esta es la clase de mensaje que podría haberse encontrado cualquiera que abriera un periódico a finales del siglo XIX. Un siglo después, el mensaje habría sido un poco menos sutil: “Enorme polla, 80 kilos, busco un hombre duro y que no ronque, de 25 a 40 años, con brazos grandes y sin gatos. Me gustan los bolos, el teatro y el gimnasio. ¡Vamos a hacer que funcione!”. El primero es una publicación del periódico Le Chasseur Français, el segundo aparece recogido en la página de Instagram de Long Lost Personals , un auténtico archivo en papel de antiguos anuncios personales de los clasificados de antaño cuyos más de 160.000 seguidores demuestran que, en tiempos de Tinder y encuentros inmediatos, la infraestructura y los tiempos de los encuentros de antaño ejercen un enorme poder de fascinación. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El saber ya no ocupa lugar
items.description: Dice el Tao Te Ching : “El que sabe, calla; el que habla no sabe”. Quizás el que sabe algo está tan ocupado en su aprendizaje o en su trabajo que no tiene tiempo de hablar; y también puede ser que calle no por propia voluntad sino porque nadie le pregunta. En el ya consabido espectáculo colectivo de los golpes de pecho y las acusaciones a otros después del último Informe PISA he oído opinar copiosamente a expertos universales de tertulia, a catedráticos de didáctica, a consejeros autonómicos, a portavoces virulentos de partidos políticos, incluso a una ministra de Educación que no había levantado la voz hasta ahora. Lo que no he visto ni oído en ningún medio impreso o digital, televisivo o radiofónico, ha sido a ningún maestro ni maestra, a ningún profesor de instituto, y ninguno de universidad, salvo los especialistas en saberes arcanos como la Didáctica o la Psicopedagogía. Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Han empeorado todos los estudiantes por igual? Nueve gráficos sobre los datos de PISA
items.description: Cinco de cada seis países de la OCDE han empeorado sus resultados educativos, sobre todo en lectura y matemáticas, según el informe PISA publicado esta semana. España ha retrocedido más que la media de la OCDE, pero no todos los estudiantes lo han hecho por igual. A partir de los microdatos de las cuatro últimas ediciones, repasamos algunas de las claves que dejan los resultados. Seguir leyendo Metodología Los datos del análisis proceden de los microdatos de PISA de las cuatro últimas ediciones: 2015, 2018, 2022 y 2025. Las medias están ponderadas y calculadas sobre las diez puntuaciones que PISA asigna a cada alumno. El «total» es la media de las tres pruebas, un cálculo propio y no una cifra de la OCDE. En algunos de los gráficos se representan también los intervalos de confianza de cada media al 95%. Los datos también tienen cuatro cautelas: La OCDE no publicó la lectura española de 2018. El sexo no se mide igual en 2022 y 2025, así que seguir a un grupo entre ambas es indicativo. Cataluña queda fuera del desglose autonómico por las incidencias que señaló PISA. En la pregunta sobre redes sociales no responde el 21% de la muestra de 2025 frente al 11% de 2022, por lo que sus datos se dan solo para 2025.

items.title: Las chicas van un curso por delante en lectura y los chicos llevan medio año de ventaja en matemáticas
items.description: Los resultados españoles del Informe PISA de 2025 son muy malos tanto para las chicas como para los chicos, pero de forma distinta. En matemáticas, las estudiantes pierden 4 puntos más que sus compañeros, un total de 18, lo que amplía a 14 su desventaja en una disciplina clave para el ámbito científico-técnico. En lectura tanto ellas como ellos experimentan el mismo batacazo: bajan 23 puntos , lo que equivale aproximadamente a un curso académico, de forma que las alumnas se mantienen 26 puntos en cabeza. En ciencias, las chicas pierden 5 puntos y los chicos 10, y la tradicional delantera de los chicos desaparece, empatando a 477 puntos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Las derecha, Junts, empresarios y sindicatos rechazan la regulación de los lobbies del Gobierno
items.description: El Gobierno sufrirá este próximo miércoles otra sonora derrota en el Congreso en la votación prevista para convalidar el decreto aprobado a finales de agosto para lograr la pendiente regulación de los lobbies en España. Salvo cambio de guion inesperado, la votación no prosperará y el decreto decaerá, con lo que pueda significar para la pérdida de una serie de millonarios fondos europeos con los que el Ejecutivo ya contaba y para la situación de los 250 lobbies inscritos en apenas 15 días. La derrota política la proporcionarán la derecha parlamentaria, PP, Junts, UPN y Vox, pero con el añadido del malestar creciente y el rechazo de la CEOE , UGT y CCOO, agentes sociales que se creían expresamente excluidos de esa regulación por figurar sus competencias en la Constitución. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Prótesis de pene, la última opción contra la disfunción eréctil: “Es un poco diferente a la erección natural”
items.description: La disfunción eréctil es un asunto que ha perturbado a generaciones de hombres durante siglos. Aparece descrito en jeroglíficos egipcios , en pinturas griegas y hasta en el Antiguo Testamento. El tema provocó desvelos a lo largo de milenios y se probó de todo para combatirla: médicos medievales lo intentaron con hierbas, oraciones y tratamientos tópicos; también se administraron afrodisíacos y en el siglo XIX, se ensayaron inyecciones de tejido testicular para aumentar la testosterona. Hoy, la disfunción eréctil está ampliamente estudiada y dispone de tratamientos que van desde pastillas, como la viagra, hasta estrategias quirúrgicas para los casos más graves. En ese abanico terapéutico, las prótesis de pene acostumbran a ser la última opción, reservada a pacientes que no responden a otros tratamientos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los vecinos de Valdebebas contra el circuito de Fórmula 1 de Madrid: “No tenemos centro de salud ni instituto y tenemos esto”
Vuelven Sandra Bullock y Nicole Kidman, las brujas que fueron demasiado brujas para el público de los noventa
items.description: En estos días de promoción de Prácticamente magia 2 , Sandra Bullock, protagonista y ahora también productora, con Nicole Kidman , de la película sobre las Owens, una familia de brujas, recordaba cómo en 1998, cuando se estrenó la primera parte, los días frente a los micrófonos no fueron tan placenteros como ahora. “No fuimos bien recibidas porque éramos demasiado brujas, demasiadas mujeres, demasiado en general”, ha recordado la actriz en varias entrevistas . Las críticas en los medios especializados fueron implacables y la taquilla, un fiasco. “Pero aquí estamos, y qué suerte tenemos de seguir para poder cosechar los beneficios y las recompensas de nuestro trabajo. Resulta que hicimos algo bonito, simplemente llegó 28 años demasiado pronto”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Una joya medieval contra el Brexit
items.description: Una joya de arte medieval está haciendo más por sanar las heridas del Brexit y acercar las dos orillas del Canal de la Mancha que una década de diplomacia. La exposición dedicada al tapiz de Bayeux en Londres, inaugurada esta semana, se ha convertido rápidamente en uno de los grandes acontecimientos culturales de la década. Con las entradas agotadas hasta 2027 a los pocos minutos después de que el British Museum las pusiese a la venta, como si fuera un concierto de Taylor Swift, la dimensión de esta muestra va mucho más allá de la cultura. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La princesa Leonor en la universidad de su octabuelo
items.description: Cuando la princesa Leonor entró esta semana a estudiar en la Universidad Carlos III, sita en Madrid, estaba ingresando en un centro de educación superior fundado en el año 1989 y bautizado en honor de Carlos de Borbón y Farnesio, Carlos III (1716-1788). Calificar el parentesco entre ambos Borbones con el vocabulario que nos ofrece el español actual nos enfrenta a un laberinto terminológico, ya que la lengua española tiene bien establecidos los términos de parentesco hasta el cuarto grado en línea recta, pero, a partir de ahí, funde y confunde términos. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Peter Sloterdijk, filósofo: “La gente que deposita su ira en la AfD perderá dinero, perderá la esperanza y perderá las ilusiones”
items.description: Todo empezó con los votantes de los nazis diciendo que estaban descontentos con lo que ocurría en el Reichstag, el Parlamento alemán. Siguió con la prensa popular clamando que aquello era una “casa de charlatanes”. Y el resultado acabó siendo el acceso al poder de Adolf Hitler . A estos episodios recurre el gran filósofo alemán Peter Sloterdijk para explicar los paralelismos que se pueden establecer entre el ascenso del Partido Nacionalsocialista Obrero Alemán (NSDAP) en los años treinta del pasado siglo y el de Alternativa para Alemania (AfD), el partido de extrema derecha alemán que la semana pasada dio el campanazo en las elecciones regionales de Sajonia-Anhalt . “La AfD, en cierto modo, es muy similar al NSDAP desde el punto de vista de esa supuesta inocuidad de sus comienzos”, dice acomodado en una butaca del hotel Eurostars Plaza Acueducto de Segovia, tras su participación en el Hay Festival de Segovia. En aquellos días, el NSDAP parecía ser un movimiento que combinaba a la perfección los principios del socialismo y el llamado “interés nacional”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Comprar y alquilar casa en 24 horas por miedo a perderla: estos son los riesgos de las operaciones exprés
items.description: Comprar o alquilar una vivienda tras una única visita de unos pocos minutos es una de las consecuencias más indeseables de la actual crisis de la vivienda. El mercado se ha vuelto acelerado, casi irracional. La falta de oferta y la presión de la demanda han instaurado las operaciones exprés y han impulsado la cultura de la decisión ultrarrápida. Y eso, cuando se trata de comprar una vivienda de cientos de miles de euros, puede ser un riesgo que arruine la economía del comprador. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Qué es la inteligencia y por qué va a acabar con nosotros
items.description: Que la inteligencia tal y como la conocemos va a acabar con nosotros es un hecho. Y lo va a hacer porque la inteligencia está mal. La noticia de los últimos días es que va a hacerlo mucho más rápido de lo que teníamos previsto porque una tecnología poderosa (llamada IA) ha acelerado el proceso. Es decir, la IA va a destruir el mundo muchísimo más rápido de lo que lo hubiéramos hecho sin su ayuda. La cuestión es por qué la inteligencia humana y su desarrollo nos conducen indefectiblemente a la extinción. Para responder a este enigma toca preguntarse por qué demonios se ha vuelto la inteligencia tan dañina. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El oscuro imperio inmobiliario de la Iglesia mormona se expande por Estados Unidos: “Son oportunistas de una manera calculada”
items.description: A tan solo 20 minutos del Aeropuerto Internacional de Denver , en una extensión de terreno baldío más grande que el Central Park de Manhattan, se extiende un ambicioso proyecto. Una nueva comunidad, denominada Tributary, está lista para levantar viviendas para más de 12.000 personas, tiendas, parques, una escuela y una estación de bomberos. Una vía férrea conectada a la zona ofrecerá acceso directo al aeropuerto, proporcionando una conexión fundamental para los suburbios adyacentes a Denver. El promotor de Tributary, Property Reserve, es relativamente desconocido para muchos de los lugareños. Pero el nombre que hay detrás es mucho más reconocible: la Iglesia de Jesucristo de los Santos de los Últimos Días (conocida popularmente como Iglesia mormona), que ha sido la propietaria del terreno durante décadas. “Están muy entusiasmados por empezar”, asegura Amy Wiles, del municipio de Aurora, donde se encuentran las 388 hectáreas del proyecto. “Es realmente una gran oportunidad para la ciudad”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Helado de leche merengada, la receta sin heladera
items.description: El nombre del helado de leche merengada no deja lugar a equívoco: leche merengada helada, en forma de sorbete de leche, por así decir. Un clásico de las heladerías y horchaterías de todo el país, la leche merengada en su versión doméstica y primigenia se trata de leche endulzada y aligerada con merengue. Congelamos esta leche merengada para obtener un delicioso helado que se suele servir con canela en polvo y que actualmente parece no gozar del mismo favor que antaño (ahora, por algo, se vende más el helado de tarta de queso). Seguir leyendo

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : L'université Nazi-Boni s'offre un complexe pédagogique moderne
items.description: L'université Nazi-Boni de Bobo-Dioulasso dispose désormais d'un nouveau complexe pédagogique moderne, doté notamment d'un amphithéâtre de 1 200 places. L'infrastructure a été inaugurée ce vendredi 11 septembre 2026 par le président du Faso, chef de l'État, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Réalisé dans le cadre de l'Initiative présidentielle pour une éducation de qualité pour tous (IPEQ), le complexe affiche une capacité globale d'accueil de 3 257 personnes et se veut un nouvel outil au service de la formation, de la recherche et de l'innovation. À l'université Nazi-Boni, les étudiants disposent désormais d'un cadre d'apprentissage qui tranche avec les infrastructures universitaires classiques. Sur le site, le bâtiment impressionne par ses dimensions et surtout par la diversité des espaces qu'il abrite. Un grand amphithéâtre de 1 200 places, quatre mini-amphithéâtres de 210 places chacun, des salles pédagogiques modulables, des laboratoires, des bureaux pour enseignants et doctorants ainsi que des salles de réunion composent ce nouveau complexe. La cérémonie d'inauguration intervient dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de l'Initiative présidentielle pour une éducation de qualité pour tous (IPEQ), qui entend notamment améliorer les conditions d'apprentissage et de travail dans les établissements d'enseignement supérieur. Selon les caractéristiques techniques présentées lors de la cérémonie, le projet est bâti sur un site d'environ 1 500 m². Il comprend deux grandes parties : un bloc amphithéâtre d'environ 1 200 places et un bloc pédagogique en R+3, destiné notamment aux activités d'enseignement, de recherche et d'administration. La coupure du ruban, marquant l'inauguration de l'infrastructure Un complexe pensé pour accueillir étudiants et enseignants Au rez-de-chaussée, le complexe abrite le grand amphithéâtre de 1 200 places, un mini-amphithéâtre de 210 places, une salle de réunion modulable, une salle de lecture, six laboratoires de travaux pratiques pouvant accueillir au total 186 personnes, ainsi que des bureaux, une cafétéria, des espaces de reprographie, des magasins et des locaux techniques. Les trois niveaux supérieurs viennent compléter cette offre. Chacun dispose notamment d'un mini-amphithéâtre de 210 places et d'une salle pédagogique modulable de 115 places. Des salles de cours, des bureaux individuels et paysagers pour enseignants, ainsi que des espaces dédiés aux doctorants sont également prévus. Pour le coordonnateur national de l'IPEQ, le Pr. Zakaria Soré, cette infrastructure traduit une volonté de faire de l'université un véritable moteur du développement national. Dans son intervention, il a rappelé plusieurs étapes de l'engagement présidentiel en faveur de l'enseignement supérieur, avant de souligner que l'infrastructure constitue la concrétisation d'une vision accordant une place centrale à la science et à la formation. « Aucun développement n'est possible sans la science », a-t-il notamment rappelé, en présentant le complexe comme une réponse aux ambitions affichées pour la modernisation du système éducatif. Une vue des futurs étudiants (nouveaux bacheliers) à la cérémonie d'inauguration La technologie au cœur du dispositif Au-delà de ses capacités d'accueil, le complexe se distingue également par ses équipements technologiques. Le grand amphithéâtre et les mini-amphithéâtres sont conçus pour pouvoir être connectés entre eux grâce à un système de sonorisation, de digitalisation et de retransmission. Cette configuration permet notamment d'organiser des enseignements ou des activités simultanément dans plusieurs salles, avec des possibilités d'interaction entre les différents espaces. Une salle de vidéosurveillance a également été aménagée afin de contribuer à la sécurité et au suivi du fonctionnement de l'infrastructure. Une application, développée avec l'accompagnement du ministère en charge de la Transition digitale, doit par ailleurs permettre de suivre le fonctionnement du complexe et de détecter rapidement d'éventuelles pannes. La question de la sécurité n'a pas été laissée de côté. Le bâtiment dispose d'un système de sécurité-incendie, de réseaux RIA et de dispositifs de détection. Les cages d'escaliers sont équipées de portes coupe-feu. Le complexe affiche une capacité globale d'accueil de 3 257 personnes L'accessibilité aux personnes à mobilité réduite a également été prise en compte. Un ascenseur d'une capacité d'au moins dix personnes dessert les différents niveaux, en complément des rampes d'accès. Le complexe bénéficie de deux principales sources d'énergie. La première est fournie par la Société nationale d'électricité du Burkina (SONABEL), avec un transformateur d'une puissance de 800 kVA. La seconde repose sur une installation solaire. À l'extérieur, des espaces de détente et d'étude ont été aménagés. Des banquettes équipées de panneaux solaires doivent notamment permettre aux étudiants de travailler de nuit. Le périmètre du complexe dispose également d'un système d'éclairage solaire autonome. Cette orientation vers les énergies renouvelables participe à la volonté de rendre l'infrastructure davantage autonome et adaptée aux besoins des étudiants. « Faire de ces amphithéâtres des lieux de révolution intellectuelle » Le complexe présente des espaces aménagées Pour le Pr. Zakaria Soré, la mise à disposition de ce complexe constitue aussi une responsabilité pour la communauté universitaire. Les enseignants-chercheurs et les étudiants sont appelés à faire de ces espaces des lieux de production de savoir, de recherche et d'innovation. « Faisons de ces amphithéâtres des lieux de révolution intellectuelle », a-t-il lancé à l'endroit de la communauté universitaire, l'invitant à produire des femmes et des hommes capables d'innover et de contribuer à la transformation de la société. La porte-parole des étudiants, Sakina Borro, a, pour sa part, exprimé la reconnaissance des bénéficiaires. Elle a présenté l'infrastructure comme un « symbole de souveraineté » et un instrument destiné à améliorer les conditions d'apprentissage. Les étudiants se sont également engagés à préserver et à valoriser le complexe afin qu'il puisse bénéficier aux générations futures. Une réalisation qui met en avant les compétences nationales La construction du complexe a également été présentée comme une opportunité économique pour les populations locales. Selon le coordonnateur national de l'IPEQ, quelque 450 ouvriers sous contrat, plus de 150 journaliers et plus de 70 femmes du village de Nasso ont participé aux différentes activités liées au chantier. Une cinquantaine d'étudiants ont également pris part aux travaux. Autre particularité mise en avant : le complexe a été conçu par un jeune agent de l'administration publique et construit par une entreprise burkinabè. Son équipement a, lui aussi, été confié aux artisans locaux, conformément à l'orientation en faveur du développement endogène. La population fortement mobilisée pour l'inauguration du complexe Pour le responsable de l'IPEQ, cette réalisation constitue ainsi une triple fierté : architecturale, économique et artisanale. Le complexe pédagogique de l'université Nazi-Boni s'inscrit par ailleurs dans une dynamique nationale plus large. Il fait partie d'une première série de 12 infrastructures actuellement en construction à travers le pays. Au total, 40 complexes infrastructurels sont annoncés dans le cadre de l'IPEQ au profit du système éducatif burkinabè. Toute chose qui permettra d'offrir aux étudiants et enseignants un environnement davantage adapté aux exigences de l'enseignement supérieur moderne. Romuald Dofini Lefaso.net

items.title: Can our votes count in 2027? — Nigerians ask
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, Regional Editor , South-West At the inauguration of the APM presidential campaign office in Ibadan last week, Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo, who is also the presidential candidate of the APM, Mr Peter Obi, the presidential candidate of NDC, Governor Bala Mohammed of Bauchi state and other opposition figures unveiled a “Reset Nigeria” agenda, where they expressed confidence that Nigerians’ votes will count in next year’s election. Read Also: Atiku won’t quit 2027 race, ADC chieftain tackles Kwankwaso This is against the backdrop of serving senators, commissioners, council chairmen and state governors openly threatening voters, opponents and dissenting residents with violence, eviction and physical harm if they refused to vote for the ruling All Progressives Party, APC. As the nation warms up to next January’s general election, some Nigerians have therefore expressed doubts that their votes would count during the election citing the unresolved glitches that occurred in the 2023 elections. They argued that the 2023 election concerns must be addressed before they could entertain any hope that the 2027 election would be different. Others submitted that the hope for a credible election must be matched with institutional safeguards and the resilience of the people to defend their votes. Unpunished electoral violence, failed tech eroding voters trust — Morris Alagoa Morris, Chief Operating Officer, Environmental Conservation Agriculture and Rural Development ECARD said: “Practically nothing has been done or said regarding penalties for electoral violence on election day. This is deeply frustrating. I am yet to read or hear of any individual appearing in court, accused of electoral violence, or being jailed as a direct consequence. “This remains the case despite the widespread violence and atrocities perpetrated during the elections, even when these acts against democracy were broadcast on live television. Given the experience of the 2023 general election, I believe it will take years to restore my lost confidence in our electoral process. INEC promised to deploy electronic transmission, but ultimately, the system proved deeply disappointing. “It is a shame and deeply unfortunate that we seem to refuse refinement and positive progress. I remain unconvinced that things will be different.” Hope alone not a strategy — Prof Okaba A university don and immediate past President, Ijaw National Congress (INC), Prof. Benjamin Okaba, said: “I share the hope that Nigerians’ votes will count in 2027, but hope alone is not a strategy. It must be backed by strong institutions, respect for the rule of law, credible electoral processes, and the determination of citizens to participate and defend democracy peacefully. It is encouraging that leaders and citizens across political divides are uniting under an agenda like “Reset Nigeria” to discuss the nation’s future. “Democracy thrives when citizens believe their participation matters and grows stronger when they demand accountability. Yet, optimism must be tempered by concern over the intimidation and violence that have marred past elections. Threatening voters or opponents for their political choices has no place in a democracy; elections should be contests of ideas, programmes, and competence, not fear, financial inducement, or brute force. INEC must learn from the shortcomings of 2023, act early and transparently, and ensure its technologies and logistics are thoroughly tested. “Security agencies must protect voters and the process, not political interests, and anyone who threatens or attacks citizens over their political choices must face the law, regardless of status. Political parties and candidates must campaign on issues, while citizens must not be intimidated: they should register, collect their PVCs, vote according to conscience, and peacefully protect their votes. Democracy is ultimately sustained by citizens who refuse to surrender their civic rights. I remain cautiously optimistic about 2027, but credible elections require collective responsibility. The reset of Nigeria must begin at the polling unit, and the choice of who leads must belong to Nigerians, determined by their votes, not by fear, violence, or money.” We must focus on issue-based campaigns — SSRG According to the Convener, South South Reawakening Group, Joseph Ambakederimo, “The most important thing for me is rhetoric built on the genuine issues bedeviling our country. In the past, people have made unacceptable remarks and statements during election campaigns, and very high-profile personalities have made comments that threatened the very fabric of the nation. “Yet, in spite of all that, the elections came, votes were counted, and winners were declared. So, regardless of whether the rhetoric is negative or positive, let us not be distracted. We must keep our eyes on the ball, which means focusing on issue-based campaigns.” Can Nigerians’ votes really count in 2027? — Amananaghan In his own submission, Tare Maureen Amananaghan, Executive Director, Fringe Voices Development Foundation said: “As an election observer, I welcome the optimism expressed by Governor Seyi Makinde, Peter Obi, Governor Bala Mohammed and other opposition leaders that Nigerians’ votes will count in 2027. “However, that optimism must be matched with concrete actions and institutional safeguards. The experience of the 2023 elections left serious concerns about transparency, result management, technology, collation and public trust. Those concerns cannot simply be wished away; they must be deliberately addressed ahead of 2027. The bigger question is not whether Nigerians will come out to vote, we have repeatedly demonstrated our willingness to participate. “The real question is whether every valid vote will be protected, accurately recorded, transparently collated and reflected in the final outcome. Concerns about political intimidation, insecurity and the shrinking space for dissent also make it necessary for INEC, security agencies, political parties, observers, the media and citizens to take greater responsibility for protecting the integrity of the process. “So, do I believe Nigerians’ votes can count in 2027? Yes, but my optimism is cautious and conditional. We should not merely hope for a credible election; we must actively work for one. Citizens must participate, observe, document and demand accountability through lawful means, while political actors must commit to peaceful competition and respect the will of the people. “Ultimately, 2027 should not only be about who wins; it should be about whether the Nigerian voter is genuinely allowed to have the decisive voice.” Votes won’t count on wishful thinking — Gbemre Coordinator, Niger Delta Peace Coalition, Zik Gbemre, said: “Making Nigerians’ votes count in 2027 cannot be achieved through slogans or wishful thinking. With the level of impunity among politicians and concerns surrounding the conduct and credibility of INEC, political permutations suggest that the desperation to win by all means necessary could escalate in 2027, which does not create an environment where votes can freely count. “Consider the reported threat by an Abuja Area Council chairman against non-APC supporters, the alleged use of thugs to prevent Peter Obi from entering Yelwata, and continuing concerns over INEC’s handling of opposition parties and access to the ballot. These developments should make every Nigerian concerned about whether the electoral process will truly guarantee that every vote is counted and reflected in the final result. “However, these odds must not discourage Nigerians from actively participating in the election; on the contrary, the people must come out in their numbers to cast their votes for candidates of their choice, not because of inducements, intimidation or political pressure, but because of their conviction that they want the best people to lead. “The resilience of the people in defending their votes, from the polling unit through collation to the final declaration of results, could ultimately make the difference and ensure that their votes count”. I foresee desperation, violence ahead — Retired Army Officer On his part, Chief Augustine Oko, a retired army officer said, “With the level of violence that is beginning to manifest, one wonders how the 2027 election will turn out. For votes to count in any election, there must be a peaceful atmosphere, and I do not foresee the prospect of that happening in 2027. “The level of desperation, brigandage, and violence that will take place will be unprecedented. The opposition talking about their votes counting certainly does not have the capacity to match what is coming. Political actors are ready to win at any cost, and with the high level of poverty, young men are willing to go to any length for just a pittance. “I only hope that Nigeria will remain after the 2027 polls.” Votes may not count without divine intervention — Educationist Madam Emmanuella Akom- Retired school principal said: ” All we can do is pray. I sympathize with the opposition, because there is no record that Nigerian voters’ votes have ever counted in any election. “We hear of people threatening to cut off hands, and others asking people to vacate certain areas if they do not support a particular party. Imagine what happened some days ago in Benue and this is just the beginning of the campaign season. I doubt most polling boxes will even reach the polling units this time. “Those responsible for guaranteeing free and fair elections are planning and tacitly supporting violence, so how can the real election be free and fair? Let us hope and pray for our country, because the suffering is too much. If democracy were practised the way we do it here, I doubt the system would have lasted this long. Nigeria is a country of particular concern, and the situation is getting worse every day”. Nigerians must pair optimism with vigilance ahead of 2027 – Akpama Cross River State Chairman of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Godwin Akpama, said: “Nigerians must approach the 2027 elections with optimism tempered by vigilance and a demand for accountability from all institutions protecting the electoral process. “The 2023 elections exposed serious weaknesses that cannot be ignored, so INEC must assure citizens that past mistakes will not recur and that every vote will be properly recorded, counted, and reflected in the final outcome. Politicians must also recognise that power belongs to the people, no party owns Nigeria, and every citizen’s right to vote according to conscience must be protected without threat, intimidation, or harassment. “The opposition has a duty to protect freely given votes by monitoring the process and insisting that announced results reflect the ballots actually cast. Resetting Nigeria also means restoring confidence in the ballot box, because democracy is weakened when citizens believe their votes do not matter. Nigerians must therefore vote, parties must protect their votes, INEC must conduct a transparent election, security agencies must remain neutral, and every institution must respect the will of the people. “Ultimately, Nigerians must be allowed to decide who governs them, that is the foundation of democracy and the confidence needed for 2027.” Former Ondo state chairman of SDP, Hon Stephen Adewale “Nigerians’ votes can count in 2027, but credible elections will not be secured by hopeful declarations alone. They will depend on the legal framework, the independence and preparedness of INEC, the neutrality of security agencies, transparent transmission and collation of results, and the determination of citizens to defend the democratic process peacefully. “The unresolved controversies surrounding the 2023 general election, particularly the failure to transmit some results electronically as expected, weakened public confidence in the electoral system. That confidence cannot be restored through assurances alone. INEC must explain what went wrong, demonstrate the improvements made since then, test its technology thoroughly and establish procedures that political actors cannot manipulate at the collation stage. Threats against voters, opponents and dissenting residents are equally dangerous. “No political leader, regardless of party affiliation or office, should be allowed to intimidate citizens or suggest that access to public services depends on electoral loyalty. Such statements should attract prompt investigation and appropriate sanctions. The optimism expressed in Ibadan is therefore desirable, but it must be matched by vigilance and institutional reform. “Votes will count in 2027 only when the institutions responsible for protecting them act transparently and impartially, and when Nigerians refuse to surrender their democratic rights to fear, inducement or intimidation”. Former Speaker, Ondo State House of Assembly and state Secretary of Afenifere, Rt Hon Bakkita Bello “When people are determined, they can stop a rolling mountain. When people are resolute, courage sets in. When people become courageous, they also become resilient. And when members of a community are resilient in the face of threats and violence, they can easily and strongly embrace vigilance and protection of their environment and votes. It happened in Osun state in the recently concluded governorship election. “The lessons learned from that may have challenged other patriots in Nigeria. The threats, intimidations and attacks, though very unnecessary and condemnable in a democracy, unleashed by the APC or any of the other parties, on perceived opponents and opposition voters, may not only generate a backlash from a dissenting public, but as well counterproductively attract sympathy and support for the opposing candidates. “To ensure that the votes count, all political Parties need to sensitise, educate, mobilise and embolden the electorates well enough and adequately.” Mr Jimoh Olufemi, Public Affairs Commentator “Without being pessimistic about the ability of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct free, fair and credible elections, I believe Nigerians’ votes can still count to a significant extent, provided opposition political parties do not remain silent in the face of electoral irregularities. “Opposition parties must be more proactive in drawing the attention of international observers and other relevant stakeholders to any practices capable of undermining the credibility of the electoral process. Silence in the face of irregularities only weakens the people’s confidence in democracy and gives room for malpractice to thrive. “We should also remind ourselves that the August 2026 governorship election in Osun State has demonstrated that credible electoral outcomes are possible when citizens are sufficiently patriotic and willing to take their civic responsibilities seriously. The responsibility for protecting the sanctity of the ballot box does not rest solely with INEC or political parties. “The electorate also has a crucial role to play by turning out to vote, safeguarding their votes and speaking up when the integrity of the process is threatened. Ultimately, the credibility of our elections will depend not only on the institutions conducting them, but also on the vigilance, courage and civic commitment of the Nigerian people.” Mr Ola Animasaun, Public Affairs Analyst “Given the seeming improvement in INEC’s preparedness during the recent off-cycle election, it is not impossible that the next general elections could represent a significant improvement over previous election cycles. “Meanwhile, INEC must ensure a level playing field before and during the elections, while political parties and their candidates must also endeavour to play by the rules. As long as the IReV (INEC Election Results Viewing) system for the transmission of election results can be effectively strengthened and made more reliable, there is no reason why the electorate should not have confidence in the overall outcome of the elections.” Comrade Ashaye Wasiu, Chairman, United Action for Democracy (UAD), Ogun State chapter “As Nigeria looks ahead to the 2027 general elections, optimism about a transparent, free, fair and credible electoral process must be matched by concrete action. Nigerians do not need more political speeches and rallies; they need civic enlightenment, voter sensitization, institutional accountability and visible reforms that restore confidence in the ballot. I agree with the call to “Reset Nigeria” and, more importantly, to “Reset INEC’s 2023 gaps.” The two are inseparable. “The credibility of the 2027 elections will depend largely on how seriously the country addresses the weaknesses exposed during the 2023 elections. At the heart of the opposition’s demand is a simple principle: let the vote be the vote. Given the allegations of intimidation, irregularities and unresolved concerns arising from 2023, that demand deserves serious consideration. “For Nigerians’ votes to truly count in 2027, at least three things must change. First is the reliability of electoral technology. BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) have become important components of Nigeria’s electoral process. Properly deployed, they can strengthen voter accreditation, improve transparency and make manipulation more difficult. But technology is only useful when it works. INEC must therefore conduct comprehensive pre-election tests, train personnel early and provide reliable backup mechanisms where network or technical failures occur. “Second is greater citizen vigilance. Voters, civil society organisations, journalists and election observers must actively monitor the process, document polling-unit results and track their transmission. Citizens should not be spectators on election day. Their participation can provide an additional layer of accountability. Third is effective enforcement of electoral laws. Vote-buying, intimidation, ballot snatching and other electoral offences must attract swift investigation and prosecution. Elections cannot be credible where offenders believe they will never face consequences. “There are, however, serious concerns that must be addressed before 2027. The first is the trust deficit. Lingering questions over the 2023 elections, coupled with threats against voters and political opponents, have weakened public confidence. The second is logistics failure. Late arrival of election materials, inadequate training of ad-hoc personnel and network challenges can undermine even the best electoral technology. “Security personnel must protect voters, INEC officials and election materials, not intimidate citizens or become instruments of partisan politics. To strengthen the 2027 elections, INEC should publish a clear post-mortem of the 2023 elections, explaining what went wrong with BVAS and IReV and what has been done to prevent a recurrence”. SDP governorship candidate in Oyo State, Mogaji Olusegun Agboola: “Nigerians have heard political promises and optimistic declarations about elections before. What matters is not what politicians say on campaign platforms, but whether the electoral environment will actually allow the people to freely choose their leaders and have their votes genuinely counted. It is easy for politicians who are positioning themselves for power in 2027 to tell Nigerians that their votes will count. The more difficult question is: what concrete steps are they taking to ensure that those votes are protected? “We cannot pretend that the concerns arising from the 2023 general election have disappeared. Nigerians witnessed serious controversies surrounding the conduct, transmission and collation of election results. Many citizens were left disappointed by the process, and the credibility questions that followed have not simply vanished because another election is approaching. So, I would rather not give Nigerians false reassurance. “I am optimistic about the Nigerian people, but I am cautious about the system. The Nigerian people are ready to vote. They have demonstrated repeatedly that they understand the power of their votes. The problem is whether the political and institutional environment will guarantee that the votes they cast are protected and faithfully reflected in the final outcome “That is what INEC must answer to Nigerians. It is not enough for INEC to tell Nigerians that their votes will count. The Commission must demonstrate, through its preparations and conduct, that every vote will be properly recorded, transmitted, collated and protected. Likewise, security agencies must understand that their responsibility during elections is to protect voters and the democratic process, not political interests. “Any attempt to intimidate voters, harass opponents or suppress dissent must be resisted, irrespective of the political party involved. I am particularly worried by the increasingly aggressive language coming from some political actors ahead of 2027. Democracy cannot survive where voters are threatened for expressing preferences different from those of people in power. No political office holder has the constitutional authority to determine who Nigerians must vote for.” “The ballot belongs to the people. “The real test of 2027 will be whether an ordinary Nigerian can walk into a polling unit without fear, cast his or her vote freely, and be confident that the vote will be counted exactly as cast. That is the standard we must demand. We must not merely hope that votes will count. We must collectively insist that they count.“ Former Ekiti State Commissioner, Lanre Ogunsuyi “The optimism expressed by opposition leaders over the 2027 elections is welcome, but Nigerians have every reason to remain skeptical, or at least be cautious. The credibility crisis surrounding the 2023 elections, the unresolved BVAS glitches, the alleged political intimidation and threats against opposition raise legitimate questions about whether the ballot will truly determine the outcome. “INEC’s promised reforms are encouraging, but technology and reforms alone cannot defeat political manipulation, regional weakness or abuse of power. Opposition parties must unite, voters must remain vigilant, and INEC must earn public trust. Nigerians should hope, but prepare to defend every vote. Nigerians should ensure, as they have done in the Osun elections, that they defend their votes after voting. It is hoped that the 2027 elections will be without glitches and the results will reflect the yearnings of the voters, such that it will not be another exercise in futility that will end in endless tribunal cases.” Let the people decide who they want – Edo IPAC chair Chairman of the Inter Party Advisory Council (IPAC) in Edo State, Bishop Akhalamhe said: “What we have observed over time is desperation among some political parties and leaders who seek power not for the people but to remain in power. If you want to lead because you see a vacuum or a knowledge gap to fill, that is acceptable but nobody should perceive you as desperate to acquire power by any means. Ultimately, it is the people that matter. “Tell them what you will do, sell your manifesto, and present good policies. If your policies are sound and people see that they are okay, why would they not vote for you? Let the people decide who they want. We must deepen democracy so that Nigerians will benefit from its dividends. Coming to power is not the issue, what the people want and what you did when you were there before is what matters.” Nigerians can make votes count – MBF The National President of the Middle Belt Forum, MBF, Dr Bitrus Pogu, has expressed confidence that Nigerians can ensure their votes count in the 2027 general elections if they remain determined to defend the electoral process. According to him, “The fact that the ruling party is becoming so nervous, attacking or threatening to attack opponents and so on, it is an indication that votes might count. That is why they are doing that. Otherwise, if they know they can just write the results and get away with it, there wouldn’t be any reason for them to intimidate the opponents. “So, if Nigerians resolve to say nothing, INEC will do anything and succeed other than doing the right thing. I believe the whole exercise and the whole ability to make things work rightly is in the hands of Nigerians.” Samuel Oyadongha; Olasunkanmi Akoni; Rotimi Ojomoyela; Peter Duru; Egufe Yafugborhi; Ozioruva Aliu; Emma Una; Ike Uchechkwu; Emem Idio; James Ogunnaike & Deola Badru also contributed to this report. Vanguard News The post Can our votes count in 2027? — Nigerians ask appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Le dirham se déprécie de 0,2% face au dollar du 3 au 09 septembre
items.description: Le dirham s'est déprécié de 0,2% face au dollar américain et de 0,7% vis-à-vis de l'euro durant la période du 03 au 09 septembre 2026, selon Bank Al-Maghrib (BAM). Au cours de cette période, aucune opération d'adjudication n'a été réalisée sur le marché des changes, indique BAM dans son récent bulletin des indicateurs hebdomadaires. Les avoirs officiels de réserve se sont établis à 502,1 milliards de dirhams (MMDH) au 4 septembre, en hausse de 0,4% par rapport à la semaine précédente et de 21,1% en glissement annuel. Concernant les interventions de BAM, elles ont totalisé, au cours de la même période, 151,1 MMDH en moyenne quotidienne. Ce volume se répartit entre des avances à 7 jours pour un montant de 55,7 MMDH, des pensions livrées à plus long terme (48,5 MMDH) et des prêts garantis (46,9 MMDH). Sur le marché interbancaire, le volume quotidien moyen des échanges s'est élevé à 3,4 MMDH et le taux interbancaire s'est situé à 2,25%. Lors de l'appel d'offres du 09 septembre (date de valeur le 10 septembre), la Banque centrale a injecté un montant de 54,6 MMDH sous forme d'avances à 7 jours. Côté Bourse, le MASI s’est apprécié de 1,7% pour se situer à un niveau proche de celui observé en début d’année. Cette évolution reflète des hausses de 4,6% pour l’indice des « Mines », de 1,7% pour celui des « Banques », de 1,4% pour les « Bâtiments et Matériaux de Constructions » et de 2,6% pour les « Services de transport ». En revanche, les indices des « Télécommunications » et de l' »Industrie pharmaceutique » se sont repliés de 2,7% et 4,9% respectivement. Pour ce qui est du volume hebdomadaire des échanges, il est revenu, d’une semaine à l’autre, de 1,8 MMDH à 1,6 MMDH, dont 1,3 MMDH réalisé sur le marché central actions et 250 millions au titre de l’opération d’augmentation de capital d’Auto Hall. The post Le dirham se déprécie de 0,2% face au dollar du 3 au 09 septembre appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Govt weighs NFC-based financial framework for Gilgit-Baltistan
items.description: GILGIT: Federal Minister for Law and Justice Senator Azam Nazeer Tarar said on Friday that consultations on the constitutional and legal status of Gilgit-Baltistan (GB) were under way, while the federal government was considering an arrangement to give the region a share in the National Finance Commission (NFC) award. The federal government currently provides annual financial grants to GB, while successive governments in the region have demanded a share in the NFC award. The federal minister said broad consultations would be held on GB’s future administrative and constitutional arrangement and all relevant stakeholders would be taken on board. According to the Ministry of Law and Jus­tice, Senator Tarar invited GB Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Advocate and Leader of the Opposition Hafiz Hafeezur Rehman to the next meeting of the GB Issues Working Group. GB Assembly backs AJK-style arrangement after CM gets cabinet approval The meeting, chaired by Senator Tarar, was attended by officials from GB, the ministries of defence, foreign affairs, and Kashmir Affairs and GB, as well as the GB Council. It discussed constitutional, legal, financial and administrative issues and reviewed previous reports, possible constitutional options and proposals for strengthening GB’s financial resources. Participants also examined practical reforms within the existing governance framework. Senator Tarar directed the working group to formulate practical proposals and prepare an interim report, along with recommendations, for the main committee. He said more time would be required to reach an agreed constitutional and legal solution, stressing that national consensus was essential. Protecting the rights of GB’s people and ensuring their sense of equality, he added, remained a priority. AJK-style arrangement Meanwhile, the GB Assembly unanimously approved a proposed financial agreement between the federal and GB governments, modelled on the financial arrangement between the federal government and Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK). Chief Minister Amjad Hussain Advocate moved the proposal in the assembly on Friday. The GB cabinet had already approved it. The chief minister said the GB government had sought federal assistance to address its budget deficit and that a committee constituted by the Prime Minister’s Office had subsequently examined a mechanism for providing the region a share in the NFC. He said the federal finance division had raised an objection that GB could become a member of the NFC only after a constitutional amendment because the region was not a constitutional part of Pakistan. As a result, he said, an NFC arrangement could not be established before such an amendment. The finance division had suggested that, until then, GB could adopt an arrangement similar to the one in place for AJK, subject to approval by the GB Assembly and adoption by the federal government. The arrangement would remain in force until GB became a constitutional part of Pak­istan and was included in the NFC, he said. The chief minister said GB faced a financial shortfall of around Rs17 billion against its estimated requirement of Rs320bn. Under the proposed agreement, the federal government would provide Rs250bn to the region. He expressed hope that the arrangement would help meet GB’s financial requirements, improve its overall financial position and provide greater stability. “If both options are not adopted, instead of providing Rs45bn, you would be providing only around Rs100bn under the existing model,” he said. He said the AJK-style agreement should be conditional on the eventual amendment of the Constitution and GB’s inclusion in the NFC. The house unanimously approved the proposal. PM’s committee examining NFC framework Chief Minister Amjad Hussain had met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in July after assuming office and demanded a greater financial share for GB. An official told Dawn that the prime minister subsequently constituted a high-level committee, chaired by Federal Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal, to examine key financial, governance and development issues concerning the region. The committee has reviewed GB’s long-term financial sustainability, hydropower development, power-sector reforms, climate resilience, digital connectivity, public service delivery and development priorities. According to the official, a key focus is developing a transparent resource-sharing mechanism based on NFC principles to ensure fair and predictable fiscal transfers to GB. The committee is expected to propose an NFC-based financial framework. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

items.title: Group in Yemen used Claude AI for missile projects, Anthropic says
items.description: • Identifies cell of threat actors running three weapons development programmes • Claims it banned accounts as soon as it detected illegal activity PARIS: A group in Yemen attempted to use Anthropic’s Claude chatbot to build guided rockets and missiles, the US firm has revealed, as Houthi forces are on the offensive in the country. In a report published on Thursday on how it had prevented illegal uses of Claude in several countries, the leading US AI firm said it had “identified a cell of threat actors based in northern Yemen running three weapons development programmes”. Those were “a guided rocket that used a commodity phone-class flight computer with final-phase homing guidance; a multi-stage ballistic missile with a stated range goal above 2,000 kilometres (1,250 miles); and a multi-variant missile… that included a hypersonic glide vehicle variant”. The cell used Claude to develop guidance, navigation and control software for the airborne weapons that would have otherwise required a team of engineers. “We do not have evidence the actors succeeded in fielding an operational device; but they did test-fire a guided rocket,” Anthropic said. “This field test appears to have failed: within hours, the actors returned to Claude to work out why it failed.” Anthropic said it had banned the relevant accounts as soon as it had detected the illegal activity. While the company did not identify the actors in question, it is likely to involve the Houthis, who control much of northern Yemen, including the capital, Sanaa. The revelation comes at a time when the Houthi rebels have launched a wide-ranging offensive across the country towards the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait, which connects Europe to Asia. On Friday, the Houthis claimed control of a Red Sea island in the middle of the Bab al-Mandeb shipping lane, completing their push to control the area. Meanwhile, Anthropic also broke up attempts to use its Claude models to develop biological weapons and carry out a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign against Ukraine. It accused Chinese competitors of hacking attempts aimed at extracting Claude’s capabilities in its report. Two Anthropic researchers warned this week that rapidly progressing artificial intelligence could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

items.title: ‘If God saves me, I’ll never drink again’ – Survivor of Ondo herbal drink tragedy
items.description: By Dayo Johnson, AKURE A survivor has said he would never drink again if God saves him, just as the death toll from suspected consumption of adulterated herbal drinks in parts of Odigbo Local Government Area of Ondo State continued to rise. Read Also: Diphtheria: Abuja barber’s ‘surgery’ made child bleed to death Meanwhile, the male seller of the toxic drink has allegedly been arrested. Fatalities were recorded in Odigbo town, Newtown, Orita, and Araromi-Obu, throwing the affected communities into mourning. Over 30 persons have died while more than 50 others are hospitalized following the consumption of the toxic drink. Confirming the incident, Chairman of Odigbo Local Government, Adegoroye Taiwo, said: “A suspect alleged to have sold the herbal drink has been arrested and handed over to the police in Akure.” He added that further investigation into the source of the substance was ongoing. Adegoroye said preliminary findings by medical experts and toxicologists indicated the deaths were linked to consumption of adulterated locally made alcoholic drinks. He pointed out that the state government deployed a medical team from Akure after he alerted Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa. According to him, the team includes officials from NAFDAC and the World Health Organisation. The Council has banned the sale and consumption of locally made alcohol and directed security agencies to arrest and prosecute violators. “Those people that died consumed toxic alcohol. People call it Jeji, Ere, giving it different names,” he explained. According to the chairman: “Those drinks that are not approved by NAFDAC, like ogogoro and ethanol, were the primary suspects based on the results of the toxicologists.” He noted that while information earlier suggested about 27 deaths and 30 hospitalizations, the medical team would provide official figures. Survivor narrates experience Meanwhile, narrating his ordeal, a 32-year-old survivor, Shola Adebayo, said he lost his sight after consuming a locally made drink known as “Monkey Tail”. Adebayo said he took two shots after a friend brought the drink from Ore. The next day, he could no longer see properly. “I took Monkey Tail. On Saturday, I discovered I couldn’t see very well, so I called my sister and I was taken to the hospital. I’m getting better, but I’m praying for my eyes. “If God saves me, I swear I will never take any drinks again. Even beer, I won’t take,” the survivor pleaded. A relative of some victims, Adebayo Adetayo Adedeji, said the community lost three young men including his cousin and two friends. He identified them as Leo, Bidemi, and Matthew. “The death of Bidemi was particularly painful because the young man was not known to be suffering from any illness before he suddenly complained of dizziness and died,” he said. Adedeji commended the LG’s ban, saying: “If they had not banned the drinking or selling of alcohol in the local government, by now Odigbo would have been a death depot.” The traditional ruler of Odigbo Kingdom, Oba Dr. Rufus Akinrimade, dismissed claims that the deaths were linked to a cultural taboo. “At the end of the day, we realised it was caused by taking different alcoholic substances, locally made alcohol. I think the deaths were caused by the intake of alcohol,” the monarch said. Oba Akinrimade urged residents, especially youths, to be careful about what they consume and to know the source of substances entering their bodies. Health authorities said investigations are ongoing. Vanguard News The post ‘If God saves me, I’ll never drink again’ – Survivor of Ondo herbal drink tragedy appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Sherry Rehman raises alarm over child abuse crisis
items.description: • Says 1,914 cases of violence and abuse against children were reported from January to June 2026 • Urges speedy trials, strict punishment for perpetrators ISLAMABAD: PPP Vice President Senator Sherry Rehman on Friday expressed deep concern over what she called a “serious child protection crisis” in Pakistan, citing 1,914 reported cases of violence and abuse against children between January and June 2026. “There can be no impunity for those who prey on children,” she said in a statement. “The scale of these cases is deeply disturbing. We are talking about children who should be protected by their families, communities and the state, yet are instead becoming victims of violence and abuse. This cannot be treated as a series of isolated incidents. It requires an urgent and coordinated response.” Punjab accounts for 80pc of cases Senator Rehman noted that 80 per cent of the reported cases were from Punjab, raising questions about the effectiveness of existing child protection mechanisms. “These figures must prompt a closer examination of whether children are able to report abuse safely, whether protection institutions are adequately equipped, and whether perpetrators are being effectively brought to justice,” she said. She said the most disturbing aspect was that 43pc of the accused were known to the victims, while nearly 45pc of incidents reportedly took place inside children’s own homes. “The home is supposed to be the first line of protection for a child. When abuse takes place behind those doors, we have to ask very difficult questions about vigilance, safeguards and accountability within families and communities,” she added. According to the data cited by Ms Rehman, 57pc of cases were reported from urban areas and 43pc from rural areas. “Child abuse does not belong to one class, one locality or one community. It is a societal problem. We have to build systems of protection that work everywhere and for every child,” she said. The senator said the registration of 89pc of reported cases with the police was encouraging, but stressed that registration must be followed by investigation and prosecution. “Registration is only the beginning. Every reported case must be investigated promptly, prosecuted effectively and pursued to its logical conclusion. Where guilt is established, perpetrators must face strict and exemplary punishment under the law,” she said. ‘Speedy trials’ Ms Rehman urged the higher judiciary to ensure speedy trials in cases involving serious crimes against children, warning that delays could deepen a sense of impunity and further traumatise victims. “Justice delayed in cases of violence against children is not simply a procedural failure. It can become another form of injustice for the child,” she added. ‘Shared responsibility’ She said protecting children was a shared responsibility of the state and society, and urged parents and guardians to remain vigilant. “Parents must remain alert, but we cannot place the entire burden of protection on families. The state has a constitutional and moral responsibility to create an environment where children can live without fear of violence, exploitation or abuse,” she added. “If, as a state, we cannot guarantee our innocent children their fundamental right to safety and protection, then we must ask ourselves what kind of future we are building. Protecting that right is not optional; it is a fundamental responsibility of the state and society,” Senator Rehman concluded. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026

items.title: À Indianapolis, la communauté nigérienne des États-Unis célèbre son unité, sa culture et son engagement…
items.description: La communauté nigérienne des États-Unis s’est retrouvée à Indianapolis, dans l’Indiana, à l’occasion d’un grand rassemblement organisé par le Conseil des Nigériens aux États-Unis d’Amérique (CONUSA), sous le thème : « Ensemble pour une diaspora unie et engagée ». La rencontre a réuni plusieurs centaines de Nigériens et Nigériennes venus d’une douzaine d’États et de différentes localités des États-Unis. Durant toute la journée, la musique, les couleurs, la gastronomie et les traditions du Niger ont occupé une place centrale, dans une ambiance à la fois festive, fraternelle et communautaire. Un pique-nique sous le signe de la convivialité La première partie du rassemblement s’est déroulée autour d’un grand pique-nique communautaire, marqué par des activités sportives, des échanges et des séances de networking entre les participants. Ce moment de détente a permis aux membres de la diaspora venus de différents États de se retrouver, de faire connaissance et de renforcer les liens qui les unissent. La gastronomie nigérienne était également largement représentée. Les participants ont pu déguster plusieurs spécialités du pays, notamment le dambou, le suya ou dibi, le foura, le doungourin damo, le fankassou, le farimassa et le massa, auxquels se sont ajoutés plusieurs autres mets traditionnels. La diversité des plats proposés a donné au pique-nique une véritable dimension culturelle et familiale. Le taekwondo nigérien fait sensation Parmi les activités de la journée figurait une présentation d’un club de taekwondo dirigé par des Nigériens. La démonstration a permis de mettre en valeur le dynamisme de la communauté dans le domaine sportif et les valeurs de discipline et de persévérance véhiculées par cette discipline. Ce moment a également été marqué par la graduation du président du Bureau Executif Federal du CONUSA, M. Moctar Mayaki, à la ceinture noire, une distinction accueillie avec enthousiasme par les participants. Sani Issa et Bachir Almagir, témoins de l’histoire du CONUSA La seconde phase de la manifestation a été consacrée à une soirée de gala, au cours de laquelle les participants ont pu découvrir davantage le CONUSA, son histoire, son organisation et son fonctionnement. Pour cette séquence, les organisateurs ont fait appel à deux personnes ressources de la communauté nigérienne des États-Unis : M. Sani Issa et M. Bachir Almagir. Tous deux ont vécu de près l’évolution structurelle de la communauté nigérienne aux États-Unis et disposent, de par leur parcours et leur implication, d’une connaissance approfondie de son histoire. Leur témoignage a ainsi permis de donner aux participants un éclairage particulièrement utile sur les différentes étapes ayant conduit à la création du CONUSA, les raisons de sa mise en place, son évolution et son mode de fonctionnement. Leurs interventions ont constitué un véritable rappel historique pour les anciens et une occasion d’apprentissage pour les nouvelles générations de la diaspora. Les différentes structures du CONUSA présentées La soirée a également été l’occasion de présenter aux participants les différentes composantes de la structure, notamment le Bureau Exécutif Fédéral, la Commission des Affaires juridiques et de contrôle (CAJ/C) et le Conseil Consultatif. M. Inoussa Moussa, président de la Commission des Affaires juridiques et de contrôle, a expliqué le rôle de sa commission, notamment en matière de transparence dans la gestion des ressources du CONUSA et de conformité des activités de l’organisation avec ses textes. De son côté, M. Ayouba Hassoumi Moussa, trésorier général, a présenté le mécanisme de collecte des cotisations ainsi que le système d’allocation de délégués aux différentes sous-sections. Ces présentations ont permis aux membres de la communauté de mieux comprendre les mécanismes de fonctionnement de leur organisation et les responsabilités confiées à chacune de ses instances. La transmission des langues au cœur des préoccupations La question de la transmission culturelle aux enfants de la diaspora a occupé une place importante au cours de la rencontre. M. Nassirou Oumarou, président de la sous-section locale de Philadelphie, a notamment appelé les parents à faire de la maîtrise des langues nigériennes une priorité dans l’éducation de leurs enfants. Son intervention a mis en évidence un enjeu majeur pour la diaspora : permettre aux nouvelles générations, nées ou ayant grandi aux États-Unis, de conserver un lien solide avec leurs racines linguistiques et culturelles. Dans le même esprit, une session de questions-réponses sur les langues et la culture nigériennes a été organisée pour les enfants. Animée par Mme Amina Tahirou, secrétaire chargée de la promotion de la femme et de l’enfant, cette activité a permis aux plus jeunes de tester leurs connaissances dans une atmosphère ludique. Des cadeaux ont été remis aux enfants ayant fourni les bonnes réponses, encourageant ainsi leur intérêt pour les langues, l’histoire et la culture du Niger. Un défilé de mode célébrant la diversité du Niger La richesse culturelle du pays a également été mise en valeur à travers un défilé de mode traditionnel, présentant les différentes composantes culturelles et ethniques du Niger. La rubrique a été animée et présentée par Mme Rachida Nabangui, secrétaire chargée de l’organisation, Mme Jamila Mayaki, membre de la sous-section de l’Indiana et du comité d’organisation, et Mme Nafissa Salihou, ambassadrice et promotrice de la culture Nigérienne. Les différentes tenues présentées ont permis de mettre en lumière la diversité des traditions vestimentaires nigériennes et de rappeler que cette diversité constitue une richesse fondamentale du patrimoine national. Aïcha La Nigérienne et Hassane Boukary mettent le feu à la soirée La soirée de gala a connu plusieurs moments artistiques très appréciés du public. La célèbre humoriste Aïcha La Nigérienne a notamment repris son titre très populaire « Goudou », une œuvre qui évoque avec humour et réalisme le quotidien de la diaspora, ses réalités, ses habitudes et certaines situations auxquelles les Nigériens vivant à l’étranger peuvent facilement s’identifier. Sa prestation a provoqué rires et enthousiasme au sein du public, qui a particulièrement apprécié cette évocation humoristique de la vie quotidienne des Nigériens hors du pays. Sur le plan musical, Hassane Boukary a également offert plusieurs chansons aux participants. Parmi les titres interprétés figurait son incontournable « Niger », considéré comme l’un de ses morceaux phares et qui a particulièrement mobilisé le public. La musique et l’humour ont ainsi contribué à donner à la soirée une atmosphère chaleureuse et profondément nigérienne. Un hommage à la communauté nigérienne de l’Indiana Un moment spécial a été consacré à la communauté nigérienne de l’Indiana, dont l’implication a été déterminante dans l’accueil et la réussite de ce grand rassemblement. Cette rubrique spéciale de remerciement a été présentée par le Vice President du B. E. F CONUSA M. Abdoul Moumouni Gado, dit « Benjamin ou Ir Niger Labizey », figure connue de la communauté. Dans son intervention, il a adressé ses remerciements à l’ensemble des membres de la communauté nigérienne de l’Indiana pour leur implication, leur disponibilité et les efforts consentis dans l’organisation et l’accueil des participants venus de différents États. M. Abdoul Moumouni Gado a également tenu à remercier particulièrement M. Souleymane Abdoul Karim, président de la sous-section du CONUSA de l’Indiana, pour son leadership, son engagement et son rôle dans la mobilisation de la communauté locale autour de cet important rendez-vous. Le président du B. E. F CONUSA, M. Moctar Mayaki, a également adressé une dédicace officielle aux différents business et entrepreneurs nigériens ayant sponsorisé l’événement, reconnaissant ainsi leur contribution à la réussite de cette grande rencontre communautaire. Une journée pour célébrer l’identité nigérienne Du pique-nique à la soirée de gala, des activités sportives au défilé de mode, de la gastronomie aux prestations artistiques, cette journée aura été une véritable célébration de l’identité nigérienne aux États-Unis. Elle aura surtout permis de réunir une communauté dispersée géographiquement mais liée par une histoire, une culture et des valeurs communes. La forte participation venue de plusieurs États américains témoigne de la volonté des Nigériens de renforcer les liens entre les différentes sous-sections, de favoriser les échanges et de construire une diaspora davantage organisée et solidaire. L’accent mis sur la transmission des langues et de la culture aux enfants, la présentation du fonctionnement du CONUSA, les échanges sur la transparence et la gouvernance, la promotion des artistes, des sportifs, des entrepreneurs et des traditions nigériennes ont donné à ce rassemblement une dimension qui dépassait largement le cadre festif. À Indianapolis, le Niger était présent dans les plats, les vêtements, les langues, la musique, l’humour, le sport et surtout dans les cœurs. Ce grand rassemblement aura ainsi porté un message fort: malgré les distances qui séparent les Nigériens à travers les États-Unis, l’unité, la solidarité et l’attachement à la culture peuvent constituer le socle d’une diaspora forte et engagée. « Votre voix. Notre force. Notre avenir. » Une devise qui aura trouvé tout son sens à Indianapolis, où plusieurs centaines de Nigériens et Nigériennes se sont retrouvés pour célébrer ce qui les unit et réfléchir ensemble à l’avenir de leur communauté. Par Oumar Moussa Toure Secretaire General du Bureau Executif Federal du Conseil des Nigeriens aux Etats Unis d’Amérique ( B. E. F CONUSA) bef_conusa@hotmail.com L’article À Indianapolis, la communauté nigérienne des États-Unis célèbre son unité, sa culture et son engagement… est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: JUI-F agrees to join PTI-led multi-party opposition moot
items.description: • PTI delegation meets Fazl; both sides discuss joint strategy on national issues • Opposition leaders to review conference preparations on 15th ISLAMABAD: The JUI-F on Friday agreed to participate in the multi-party conference (MPC) being organised by the PTI ahead of its long march to Islamabad on Sept 27. A PTI delegation met JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman at his residence to woo the religio-political party to join its anti-government drive. Both sides discussed the possibility of a joint opposition strategy on key national issues. The PTI delegation comprised party chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan, general secretary Salman Akram Raja and former National Assembly speaker Asad Qaiser. Talking to the media after the meeting, Barrister Gohar said opposition parties would adopt a joint strategy inside parliament. “We will take all political parties into confidence on national issues,” he said, adding that an MPC would be convened to discuss important issues, including the creation of new provinces. “Today’s meeting was very important,” Barrister Gohar said, adding that the opposition would formulate its future strategy through a united platform. Regarding the PTI’s planned long march, Barrister Gohar said it was aimed at seeking justice and would remain peaceful. Responding to a query about the Maulana declining to join the Sept 27 protest, he clarified that the PTI delegation had not visited the JUI-F chief’s residence to formally invite him to participate in the march. ‘Wave of unrest’ Speaking on the occasion, JUI-F leader Maulana Abdul Ghafoor Haideri said several issues came under discussion, including consultations on convening the MPC and the creation of new provinces. He said a wave of unrest had gripped Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and such matters would be discussed at the MPC. “Patriotic political parties will play their role and we will evolve a joint strategy,” Mr Haideri said, adding that political forces inside and outside parliament would be approached to participate in the conference. He added that people across the country were facing serious inflation, while unr­­est and distress were growing. He also anno­unced that the JUI-F was holding workers’ conventions across the country. According to a statement issued by the opposition alliance, the Tehreek-i-Tahafuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP), the PTI delegation met the JUI-F chief at his residence, where the two sides held detailed discussions on the MPC and the PTI’s Sept 27 protest call. The two sides also discussed “strengthening of the country’s constitutional and democratic systems”. “The leaders also discussed the need for mutual consultation and a joint str­u­­ggle among political parties to uphold the supremacy of the Consti­tution and the rule of law, and to safeguard democratic principles in the country,” the statement added. Review meeting on 15th Separately, TTAP chief and Opposition Leader in the National Assembly Mehmood Khan Achakzai said on X that he and Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas held a meeting with PTI leaders, including Barrister Gohar, during which it was decided to hold the MPC “at the earliest”. According to a statement, the opposition leaders decided to meet on Sept 15 to review progress on the MPC. They also agreed to contact political parties “as soon as possible” to convene the conference. The opposition leaders also held consultations with Mr Achakzai on the Sept 27 march. Mr Acha­kzai and Mr Abbas directed the PTI to make full preparations for the protest. Published in Dawn, September 12th, 2026
